narratives.DontHandRoll:
Problem: AI opponent logic
Use: Minimax algorithm (implement directly — no library needed for TTT)
Rationale: Tic-Tac-Toe has only 9 cells and a shallow game tree; minimax is simple, fast, and well-documented. External game-AI libraries add complexity with no benefit here.

Problem: CLI output / terminal UI
Use: Standard library (fmt/print) — no TUI framework needed
Rationale: TTT board display is simple enough that a 3x3 grid renders fine with plain print statements. A TUI library (e.g. tview, Rich, Spectre.Console) is overkill unless the UI needs animation or color themes.

Problem: Web UI (if web target chosen)
Use: A thin framework matching the chosen language (e.g. htmx+Go, Flask+Jinja2, or Blazor for C#)
Rationale: A full SPA framework (React, Angular) is heavy for a 3x3 grid. Choose the lightest option that matches your language.
narratives.CommonPitfalls:
Pitfall: Missing draw detection
What: Game loop runs forever when board is full with no winner
Why: Win check passes but no full-board check
Avoid: After every move, check win first; if no win and board is full, it's a draw
Warning signs: Game never ends without a winner in tests

Pitfall: Incorrect win detection
What: Win check misses diagonals or columns
Why: Only rows are checked, or array indices are off-by-one
Avoid: Write explicit checks for all 8 win lines (3 rows, 3 cols, 2 diagonals); cover each with a test
Warning signs: Agent wins horizontally but not diagonally in manual play

Pitfall: State mutation in minimax
What: AI search corrupts the real board state
Why: Minimax modifies the board in place and fails to restore it
Avoid: Copy the board before each recursive call, or pass an immutable copy
Warning signs: After the AI plays, the board shows extra or wrong markers

Pitfall: No input validation
What: Player can enter a cell index that is out of range or already occupied
Why: Happy-path code skips boundary and occupancy checks
Avoid: Validate move before applying it; re-prompt on invalid input
Warning signs: Crash or silent overwrite on bad input
